text:
Matthew Tkachuk played only 31 games last season, and this fall has been a reminder of what Florida was missing. He has 32 points in 24 games, 25 of them assists, and 18 on the power play. NHL.com's notebook highlighted his point streak, which was still going after a two-goal night against Edmonton on Nov. 17. A few days earlier in St. Louis, he called a tribute to his father "Icing On The Cake," per NDTV Sports.

He's a setup man first right now. His 7 goals came on 6.4 expected, so the finishing is honest, and the playmaking is the engine: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 95th percentile among forwards, carrying the puck in on 69% of his entries (from just six tracked games). Florida has 55.2% of 5v5 expected goals, the quality of chances, with him on the ice. And with his brother Brady traded to the Panthers in June, the Tkachuks finally share a bench. Our numbers project about 95 points.
headline: Matthew Tkachuk is setting the table again
